premises: Lattice mismatch at the metal/oxide interface governs oxide stability via misfit dislocations.
A critical threshold density of misfit dislocations is required to prevent cracking and spallation.
Elemental substitution (e.g., Si) can reduce lattice mismatch and increase dislocation density.
In situ TEM can quantify misfit dislocation density and correlate it with oxide cracking.
